summary: The SDK incorrectly rejects fiber-based activity executors on Ruby 4.0+ due to a version check that doesn't account for major versions greater than 3, preventing users from using fiber executors on newer Ruby versions.
userImpact: Users cannot use fiber-based activity executors on Ruby 4.0 or later due to an incorrect version check, preventing them from accessing optimized concurrency features.
rootCause: The `fibers_supported` method contains a version check that only evaluates the minor version and assumes a major version of 3, causing it to reject Ruby 4.x versions.
proposedFix: Update the `fibers_supported` method to allow Ruby 3.3+ and all Ruby 4.x: `major > 3 || (major == 3 && minor >= 3)`
workaround: Monkey-patch the version check in application code (example: https://github.com/jasonligg/temporal-samples-ruby/blob/00100335e19d973a07c13e46ea95ca713928e04e/fiber_activity/worker.rb#L12-L25)
resolutionDetails: The version check in the `fibers_supported` method was updated to correctly handle Ruby 4.x versions.
keyQuote: The version check only evaluates the minor version and assumes a major version of 3, which causes it to incorrectly reject Ruby 4.x.
